clue.text: Correct uniform for the Emperor's anniversary?

definitions.text: Correct uniform for the Emperor's anniversary?

parts.words: Correct uniform for the Emperor's anniversary?
parts.note: the emperor of the fairy tale paraded in nothing at all, so his proper outfit is bare skin, and 'anniversary' points to the day of birth

explanation.surface: A court tailor wonders what the Emperor should wear for his jubilee celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emperor is the one in Hans Christian Andersen's tale of the new clothes, who walked out naked; the answer is the jokey name for nakedness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for nakedness, the state one is born in, which the naked Emperor wore.

clue.text: Queasy, one has taxi pulled up, finding bugs

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the word for taxi is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
queasy means ill
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A carsick passenger has the taxi stop and turns out to have caught an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' fits a down clue: the taxi word is read upwards. 'Queasy' looks like part of the surface story but supplies the illness piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, and bugs is the informal word for germs that cause illness.

clue.text: Head off, going behind the barrier

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so taking the head off drops the opening letter

parts.note: trailing means going behind, following at the rear

explanation.surface: Someone is told to set off and follow behind the barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like an instruction to leave; it removes the T from TRAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence of rails, a kind of barrier that blocks the way.

clue.text: The arrogant swine show stilettos

parts.note: high, as in high and mighty, can mean arrogant
heels is an old word for cads or swine, contemptible men

explanation.surface: Proud, nasty people show off their pointed footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' is plural here, matching HEELS, the dated slang for rotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilettos are shoes with very tall thin heels, a type of the footwear named.

clue.text: A form of ludo intended for audience

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a form of a word is its letters reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A version of the board game ludo is meant to be played in front of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' signals a rearrangement of the board game's name. Ludo is a simple dice-and-counter board game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken out loud means said so that listeners can hear, meant for an audience.

clue.text: Director's always breaking troubled rest

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the other letters to sit inside them
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of rest are rearranged

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A film director is always interrupting a disturbed night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the letters of rest, and 'breaking' splits that result to take in the poetic word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: A steerer is one who guides or directs the course of something, a director in the plain sense.

clue.text: A national drink

definitions.meaning: a national is a citizen of a particular country, here one from Rome or Milan
... vermouth, often just called It, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A citizen of some country orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is the British name for gin mixed with Italian vermouth, so the nationality doubles as the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Italy is one example of a national; Italian vermouth is the drink.

clue.text: One of our staff shows intelligence over questions, a lot incomplete

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: intelligence in the sense of information, news
an exam paper is a set of questions

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: A newspaper's employee is shown questions and much else unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the Y from MANY to give MAN. 'our staff' is the newspaper speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist working for a paper is one of that newspaper's staff, as the paper itself says.

clue.text: Attractive, though it's not fine eating out here

indicators.note: it's not says the following letter is missing from the word

parts.note: fetching means attractive
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A restaurant looks appealing, though it is not a good place to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating out here' looks like dining, but it is acid eating into a metal plate; 'it's not' removes F from FETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: In this printmaking process acid eats away lines in a metal plate, so the eating out happens here.

clue.text: Finished a jolly sort of service

parts.note: over means finished
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A cheerful kind of church service has just ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like cheerful, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis or cricket, a ball delivered with the arm above the shoulder is this kind of serve or delivery.

clue.text: Sign thus and attain distinction

definitions.meaning: someone who cannot write signs with a cross, putting down a mark
to become successful and well known

explanation.surface: A person signs a document this way and becomes famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become notable, while literally it describes signing with a cross.

clue.text: Work at Billingsgate, we hear, for personal gain

indicators.note: we hear means the words are taken as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: Billingsgate is London's fish market, so the work there is to sell fish

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job at the fish market only to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market; 'sell fish' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out of self-interest is doing things for personal gain, the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Crane to see boy

definitions.meaning: a lifting machine with a long arm, as on a dock or oil rig
a boy's first name, short form Derek

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a dockside crane to meet a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of crane used for lifting cargo and also a man's first name.

clue.text: Copying small brooch in silver

indicators.note: in means the brooch piece goes inside the silver piece

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pin is a small brooch

explanation.surface: A jeweller is imitating a little silver brooch.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying someone's manner is imitating them, as an ape mimics; the verb form matches.

clue.text: One's pater is distressed by common language

indicators.note: distressed means upset or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A father is upset by everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is distressed' rearranges the nine letters of ONE'S PATER. Pater is old public-school slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: This invented tongue was designed as a common international language for all peoples.

clue.text: Do row, creating official policy

parts.note: a do is a party
a row, as in a line of people or things

explanation.surface: A celebration descends into a quarrel and produces a formal policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The stance officially laid down by a political party is the position its members must follow.

clue.text: One who won't allow spirits on the premises

definitions.text: One who won't allow spirits on the premises

parts.words: One who won't allow spirits on the premises
parts.note: reads as a teetotal landlord refusing alcohol, but the spirits are ghosts being driven out of a house

explanation.surface: A strict landlord bans liquor from the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who expels evil spirits or ghosts from a person or place does not let spirits stay.

clue.text: Odd topic cut short at the back of one's brain

indicators.note: odd means strange or unusual, so the letters are rearranged
cut short means the word cut loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A strange subject is trimmed at the back of someone's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CUT to CU, and 'Odd' rearranges TOPIC plus CU.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical term names the back part of the head or skull, behind which the brain sits.

clue.text: Rook is cold, but getting warmer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a heater is a device that warms

explanation.surface: A chess piece is cold but is warming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece or the bird; as a noun it also means a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, so a rook is a cheat or swindler.

clue.text: Stick to foie gras

definitions.meaning: glue, an adhesive used to stick things
a goose-liver spread, a smooth pâté

explanation.surface: Someone sticks with the goose-liver pâté.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive glue is called by this name, and so is a smooth meat spread such as foie gras.

clue.text: Scanner required for every employer

parts.note: per means for each, for every
an employer here is one who employs, i.e. uses something

explanation.surface: A security scanner is needed for each company boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' looks like a boss, but it is one who employs a thing, a user.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a text is to read it over, and one who reads closely like that is this person.

clue.text: Examine boy standing up in disgrace

parts.note: to scan is to examine

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word for boy is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a boy who has been shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' suits a down clue: the word for boy is read from bottom to top beneath the word for examine.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public disgrace, an event causing shame and outrage.

clue.text: Satirists put them on with disas-. trous effect

definitions.meaning: people who mock or ridicule, satirists

definitions.text: put them on with disas-. trous effect
definitions.meaning: British slang for jinxing it, making it go wrong

explanation.surface: Satirists bring about a disastrous result.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put the mockers on' something is British slang for jinxing or spoiling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockers are people who ridicule; in the slang idiom they bring bad luck when put on.

clue.text: Unctuous senior citizen accepted by the fringes of society

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so one piece sits inside the other
the fringes are the outer edges, the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: OAP is old-age pensioner, a British senior citizen

explanation.surface: An oily old pensioner is let in by the outskirts of polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fringes of' society gives S and Y, which take in OAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous means smarmy and ingratiating, like someone oily or full of soft soap.

clue.text: End of stout pole providing police with weapon

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A thick stick ends up giving police a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' looks like a last-letter instruction, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship a yard is a stout spar, and either end of it is called this.

clue.text: Pathan and horse represented a fiery mixture

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A Pathan tribesman and his horse are shown in a flaming combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges PATHAN plus H. Pathans are a people of Afghanistan and Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: This flammable oil mixture of hydrocarbons is used as fuel, a fiery mixture indeed.

clue.text: Popular drink reportedly one's not allowed to trade

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the drink is taken by its sound

parts.note: cider is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a popular drink is barred from sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone with confidential knowledge of a company is barred from insider dealing in its shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with inside knowledge of a company is legally barred from dealing in its shares.

clue.text: Dirty fuel, they say, is a portent of trouble

parts.note: dirty weather is stormy

indicators.note: they say means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: petrol is a fuel

explanation.surface: Grimy fuel is said to be a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' means foul weather, STORMY, rather than grimy.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird was said to appear before storms, so its name came to mean a harbinger of trouble.
